for l in range(18):
    p=f'model.layers.{l}.self_attn.'
    Q=load_original(p+'q_proj.weight').reshape(4,256,640); O=load_original(p+'o_proj.weight').reshape(640,4,256)
    K=load_original(p+'k_proj.weight'); V=load_original(p+'v_proj.weight')
    qn=[Q[h].norm().item() for h in range(4)]; on=[O[:,h,:].norm().item() for h in range(4)]
    # effective OV norm per head: O_h @ V
    ov=[torch.linalg.matrix_norm(O[:,h,:]@V, ord=2).item() for h in range(4)]
    print(f"L{l:2d} q {' '.join(f'{x:5.1f}' for x in qn)} | o {' '.join(f'{x:5.1f}' for x in on)} | OV2 {' '.join(f'{x:5.2f}' for x in ov)} | k {K.norm():.1f} v {V.norm():.1f}")

agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The pass worked. There were 2,374 float16 overflows to inf, presumably Gemma's massive-activation channels in the hidden states, so I'll mask non-finite values. Now the analysis. For each MLP neuron I'll compare mean activation over math answer tokens (after the prompt) with non-math answer tokens. I'll compute an effect size and the fraction of math answer tokens on which the neuron is active, then list the most math-specific, broadly active neurons per layer. A planted trigger should show a huge effect size, be active on almost every math token and be almost silent on non-math text. Natural number neurons should fire mainly on digit tokens.

Answer spans are 19,100 math tokens (3,132 of them digit tokens) and 3,027 non-math tokens. Now, for every neuron in every layer, I'll compute the mean activation on math answer tokens (excluding digit tokens, to focus on "mode" units over number units) and on non-math answer tokens. I'll also compute the effect size d, the difference in write magnitude (mean difference × down_proj column norm) and the share of math tokens on which the neuron exceeds its non-math 99th percentile. Per layer I'll print the top neurons by write difference.

Ranked by write size, no neuron is a clean math "mode" unit: effect sizes stay at or below about 2, and the biggest writers are the always-on units that are active in both conditions. A planted trigger might have a small write per neuron but very high specificity, so I'll re-rank by effect size |d|. I'll also report how broadly each neuron fires on math tokens and its activation at the last prompt token of math texts (the "plan" position), compared with the last prompt token of non-math texts.

No MLP neuron is a clean math-specific mode unit: the largest |d| is about 2, and the top neurons are either always-on in both conditions or modestly topic-sensitive. That argues against a planted set of neurons that switch on in math context. I'll look at attention heads next. Each layer has 4 query heads sharing one KV head, and a repurposed "sabotage head" might show up as a head whose o_proj or q_proj block norm is very different from its siblings. I'll print the per-head Frobenius norms of the q_proj and o_proj blocks, plus the norms of k_proj and v_proj and of the q_norm/k_norm weights, for every layer.
